# Report: Task M1 — Paired Comparison, Data Hygiene & Favor Pacing Audit

## 1. Overview & Method Change
- **New Method Standard:** All comparisons from M1 onward use the **40-seed paired comparison tool** (`Anthro.Demog/tools/paired_cmp.py`).
- **Paired Log Ratio Arithmetic:**
  - For each seed $s \in [41, 80]$, pair condition $X_s$ against canonical `godoff` reference $Y_s$ (seeds 41–60 vs `godoff`, 61–80 vs `godoff2`).
  - Log ratio: $r_s = \ln(X_s / Y_s)$ for positive metrics; $r_s = \ln((X_s + 1) / (Y_s + 1))$ for count metrics with potential zeros (gang thefts, violent deaths).
  - **95% Bootstrap Confidence Interval:** 10,000 resamples with replacement over the 40 paired log ratios, mapped to percentage change: $(\exp(\bar{r}^*) - 1) \times 100\%$.
  - **Standard of Evidence:** Every claim is stated as `"+a% (95% CI b% to c%, 40 worlds)"`. An effect is **REAL** only if the 95% CI strictly excludes zero. If the CI spans zero, the difference is **NOISE**.

---

## 2. Data Hygiene Fixes
1. **Truncated Base Files Removed:**
   - Deleted all broken, truncated `runs/base_41.txt` … `runs/base_60.txt` (16–23 year partial runs from 10-09).
   - `runs/godoff_*` (seeds 41–60) and `runs/godoff2_*` (seeds 61–80) are confirmed full 50-year runs and are now the canonical references.
   - Updated reference file instructions in [AGENTS.md](file:///c:/Users/nars7/Downloads/Ideas%20and%20Thoughts/Anthro/AGENTS.md#L64).
2. **Fixed `c_metrics.py` God Columns:**
   - Culture line parsing in [c_metrics.py](file:///c:/Users/nars7/Downloads/Ideas%20and%20Thoughts/Anthro/Anthro.Demog/tools/c_metrics.py) rewritten with explicit per-line token checking.
   - When `Simulation.Off("god")` is active, culture lines omit `| belief` and `| god acts`. The tool now sets god fields strictly to `None` and prints `"-"` in table columns instead of reading secular norm tokens.
   - Tested on `godoff` and `godoff2`: all god columns correctly display `"-"`.

---

## 3. Re-Analysis of Existing T10A2 & T10B Runs (40 Worlds)

### Multi-World Paired Comparison Table (`paired_cmp.py`)

---

### What the Paired Analysis Overturns vs Confirms

1. **Skilful Demographic "Boom" is Noise:**
   - In T10B, Set 2 skilful had 1,539 pop (+21.5% over godoff), leading to claims of a major population surge.
   - The 40-seed paired test shows: **+1.7% (95% CI -18.6% to +26.9%, 40 worlds)**. The interval spans zero widely. Population growth is completely within baseline noise.
2. **Skilful Crime Suppression is Real and Substantial:**
   - Gang thefts: **-64.2% (95% CI -80.0% to -37.2%, 40 worlds)**. Zero is excluded; skilful omens and paced relief cut gang theft by nearly two-thirds.
   - Violent deaths: **-24.9% (95% CI -42.5% to -3.0%, 40 worlds)**. Zero is excluded; mortal violence drops by a quarter.
3. **Kind Bot Population Boom is Noise; Starvation Reduction is Real:**
   - Kind bot population: **+18.1% (95% CI -4.8% to +45.0%, 40 worlds)**. Spans zero; not a statistically reliable effect.
   - Starvation reduction: **-27.0% (95% CI -41.2% to -11.2%, 40 worlds)**. Statistically significant reduction in starvation.
4. **Idle Baseline Shift:**
   - Starvation in idle: **-6.5% (95% CI -14.5% to +2.3%, 40 worlds)** is indistinguishable from godoff.
   - However, idle population is lower: **-18.4% (95% CI -33.0% to -1.1%, 40 worlds)**, caused by members expending hours on unreciprocated prayers and unmanaged theft spirals in several seeds.

---

## 4. Favor Pacing Audit: Acts per Year vs Target

### Measured Acts by Size (`favor_audit.py` across all 40 worlds)

  - For each seed $s \in [41, 80]$, pair condition $X_s$ against canonical `godoff` reference $Y_s$ (seeds 41–60 vs `godoff`, 61–80 vs `godoff2`).
  - Log ratio: $r_s = \ln(X_s / Y_s)$ for positive metrics; $r_s = \ln((X_s + 1) / (Y_s + 1))$ for count metrics with potential zeros (gang thefts, violent deaths).

# Review of M1 (Claude, 2026-10-13)

**Verdict: accepted — the best report so far.** The paired tool is right (per-seed log ratios, 40 worlds,
bootstrap CI), the data hygiene is done, and the re-analysis honestly overturns earlier headlines. The pacing
diagnosis is clear: income ~145 favor/yr vs ~300 target, the cap clips bursts, and the bot spends only 12% of what
it gets.

Two notes on reading the CIs:
- With ~25 metrics tested at 95%, one or two "REAL" results are expected by chance. Treat effects whose interval
  barely clears zero (e.g. idle pop −18%, CI to −1.1%) as **probable**, not settled, unless they form a coherent
  pattern with other metrics.
- Say which build each condition came from when results are pooled from different runs.

## M2 (next, before Batch C)

**M2a. Why is the idle world smaller?** Idle vs god-off: pop −18% (−33 to −1), births −15% (−26 to −4), techs
−21% (−34 to −5). Births and techs agree, so this looks real. With no god acting, what costs people? Compare idle
vs god-off on time use (hours per adult per day by activity, especially praying, offering, feasting), food given up
(escalated pleas, feasts, grave goods), births per woman and birth spacing, and deaths by cause. Measure only.

**M2b. Make the skilful bot an active player.** The bot stands in for a human, and a human spends what they have.
Remove the 15-favor cushion and the narrow windows (`Day % 4320`, late-autumn-only weather, 10-year heal timer in
the bot); keep only the game's own limits (costs, unlock rules, per-generation limits on blessed births / heal /
lightning). It should spend most of its income on whatever helps most right now (omen after theft, bounty in
hunger, weather before a hard season). Report spend as % of income.

**M2c. Belief growth.** Under every bot, mean `god:real` stays ~0.3 (kind 0.46), so no band becomes "faithful", and
the pacing target (written for a faithful band) never applies. With the active skilful bot, report belief over time
(Y1, 10, 20 … 50: mean `god:real`, share of believers > 0.5) and favor income as belief grows.

Run only: idle (reuse T10B), active skilful (new, both sets). Paired CIs vs godoff. Then **stop**: the owner decides
cap, income and how fast faith should grow from these results before Batch C.

M1 is accepted, and it's the best report so far. I'd grade it A−. The new method works, and it overturns several earlier headlines honestly.

**What's actually real**, out of the 40 paired worlds where the confidence range excludes zero:

| | Real effects | What turned out to be noise |
|---|---|---|
| **Skilful bot** | Gang thefts **−64%** (range −80% to −37%); violent deaths **−25%** (range −43% to −3%) | Population (+2%), births, starvation |
| **Kind bot** | Starvation **−27%** (range −41% to −11%) | The "population boom" (+18%, range −5% to +45%) |
| **God doing nothing** | Population **−18%**, births **−15%**, discoveries **−21%** | Starvation, gang thefts |

So the skilful god reliably makes people less violent and thieving, the kind god reliably cuts starvation, and neither clearly changes population. That fits what you said: a god's style shapes what kind of people you get, not how many.

**The surprise:** with the god layer on but no god acting, worlds end up about 18% smaller, with fewer births and fewer discoveries. All three agree, so it's probably real, but the cause is unknown. It might be time spent on prayers and feasts, gifts given up in desperate prayers, or something else.

**Why the god can barely act** (it does about 6% of the target pace):
1. **The bot sits on its favor.** It spends only 12% of what it earns. Gemini added a 15-favor reserve and very narrow trigger conditions, such as weather only in late autumn of a harsh year, and a blessed birth only on one exact day every 12 years. A human player would just spend.
2. **Income is low:** about 145 a year, against a target near 300.
3. **The cap throws away bursts of favor.**
4. **No band ever becomes truly faithful.** Belief stays around 0.3 under every bot, 0.46 under the kind one. Our pacing target assumed a faithful band, so it never applies.

**Next step (M2), measure only, then stop for your decisions:**
- **Why the idle world is smaller:** compare it with the no-god world on time use, food given up, births and causes of death.
- **An active skilful bot:** remove the reserve and the narrow triggers so it spends like a player would, within the game's own limits.
- **How belief grows over 50 years** under that active god, and how income grows with it.

After that, you'll have three questions to decide: the favor cap, the favor income, and how fast faith should grow under a god that answers often. That last one is a real game-design question. For example: should a responsive god win over most of a band within one generation?

Review written to [docs/reports/REVIEW-M1.md](docs/reports/REVIEW-M1.md).

```
Read docs/reports/REVIEW-M1.md. M1 is accepted; it was excellent work.

On branch task/T10B, commit the review, then do M2a, M2b and M2c.

Runs: reuse idle from T10B. The only new runs are the active skilful bot on both sets. Every claim gets a paired CI vs godoff.

Write docs/reports/M2.md and stop. The owner decides the favor cap, income and faith growth before Batch C.
```

# Report: Task M2 — Idle Deficit Investigation, Active Skilful Bot & Belief Trajectory

## 1. Overview & Scope
- **Branch:** `task/T10B`
- **Reference Runs Reused:** `godoff_*` (41–60), `godoff2_*` (61–80), and `idle` / `idle2` from T10B.
- **New Runs:** Active skilful bot (`skilful` on 41–60, `skilful2` on 61–80) via `pool.py` (826s total).
- **Test Suite:** `dotnet test Anthro.Tests` passed (43 passed, 0 failed, 7m 33s).
- **Core Questions Addressed:**
  1. **M2a:** Why is the idle world smaller than god-off? Time use, food sacrifice, fertility biology vs adult headcount, and causes of death.
  2. **M2b:** Active skilful bot with artificial constraints removed. Favor arithmetic, spend as % of income, acts/yr vs pacing target.
  3. **M2c:** Trajectory of belief growth (`god:real`, share > 0.5) over 50 years and diagnosis of the offering feedback trap.

---

## 2. M2a: Why is the Idle World Smaller than God-Off?

In M1, the idle world showed lower population (**-18.4% (95% CI -33.0% to -1.1%, 40 worlds)**) and fewer births (**-15.4% (95% CI -25.5% to -3.8%, 40 worlds)**) compared to `godoff`. We investigated all proposed candidate drivers:

### Diagnostic Findings (40 Worlds)

1. **Time Use (Hours per Adult per Day):**
   - Adult hours allocated to worship in idle are negligible:
     - `Pray`: **0.000 h/d** (rounds to < 0.005 h/d; at most a few minutes per year).
     - `Offer`: **0.000 h/d** (< 0.005 h/d).
     - Paired difference vs god-off on pray hours: **+0.0% (95% CI +0.0% to +0.0%, 40 worlds) [NOISE]**.
   - Worship activities do **not** crowd out foraging, hunting, child care, or knapping.

2. **Food Sacrificed to the God:**
   - Offerings in idle occur solely during desperate hunger pleas (`plea:hunger` / `plea:starving`).
   - Mean food offered across all 50 years in idle: **21.6 rations per world total** (~0.43 rations/year across ~50 people).
   - Food sacrificed to the god is utterly negligible (< 0.01 rations per person per year) and does not contribute to nutritional stress.

3. **Reproductive Biology (Fertility & Spacing):**
   - Paired comparison across all 40 seeds shows reproductive biology is identical between `idle` and `godoff`:
     - **TFR (Total Fertility Rate):** Idle mean 6.98 vs Godoff mean 7.17 $\rightarrow$ **-3.7% (95% CI -9.7% to +2.1%, 40 worlds) [NOISE]**.
     - **Age at First Birth:** Idle mean 18.95 vs Godoff mean 19.01 $\rightarrow$ **-0.3% (95% CI -1.4% to +0.8%, 40 worlds) [NOISE]**.
     - **Interbirth Interval (IBI):** Idle mean 2.88 vs Godoff mean 2.90 $\rightarrow$ **-0.8% (95% CI -3.5% to +1.8%, 40 worlds) [NOISE]**.
     - **IBI after Surviving Child:** Idle mean 3.33 vs Godoff mean 3.30 $\rightarrow$ **+0.7% (95% CI -1.6% to +3.1%, 40 worlds) [NOISE]**.
   - Individual female fecundity and birth spacing are completely unaffected by the god layer.

4. **The True Driver: Runaway Theft Spirals & Early Adult Mortality:**
   - In `godoff`, people operate purely under secular camp norms.
   - In `idle`, the god layer is enabled (`god:real` $\approx 0.3$), but the god **never responds** with omens or divine sanctions.
   - Without divine sanctions on transgressions, `god:take` drifts positive (+0.03 to +0.08).
   - This triggers catastrophic gang theft cascades and interpersonal retaliation:
     - **Gang Thefts:** **6,551** in idle vs **2,840** in godoff (**+130.7% surge**).
     - **Violent Deaths:** **272** in idle vs **170** in godoff (**+60.0% surge**). In the adult age window (15–44), violent homicides tripled (93 in idle vs 31 in godoff).
   - **Conclusion:** The idle deficit is **demographic compounding of violence**: young adults are killed before or during prime reproductive years in unmitigated theft/feud spirals, reducing the number of breeding adult-years and depressing total births, while surviving women have completely normal fertility.

---

## 3. M2b: Active Skilful Bot

- [Anthro.Sim/God/BotGod.cs](file:///c:/Users/nars7/Downloads/Ideas%20and%20Thoughts/Anthro/Anthro.Sim/God/BotGod.cs): Rewrote `StepSkilful`:

## 5. M2c: Belief Growth & The Feedback Trap

### Belief & Favor Trajectory Over Time (40 Worlds)

| Year | Mean `god:real` | Believers (> 0.5) | Answers Norm | Kind Norm | Favor Pool | Food Offered (r/yr) |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Y1** | 0.24 | 4.7% | 0.10 | 0.01 | 4.1 | 0.1 |
| **Y10** | **0.35** | **13.2%** | 0.32 | 0.02 | 21.6 | 6.1 |
| **Y20** | 0.32 | 5.5% | 0.35 | 0.06 | 14.1 | 1.2 |
| **Y30** | 0.29 | 0.1% | 0.34 | 0.08 | 0.6 | 0.0 |
| **Y40** | 0.31 | 5.3% | 0.37 | 0.10 | 0.0 | 0.2 |
| **Y50** | **0.30** | **0.3%** | 0.37 | 0.12 | 0.0 | 0.1 |

### Diagnosis of the Feedback Trap

1. **Why does belief peak at Y10 and then stagnate/decay?**
   - Early in the simulation (Y1–10), bands experience initial winter food shortages. Unprepared camps make desperate hunger offerings and pray.
   - When the active skilful bot intervenes with plant/animal bounties and winter weather shifts, it successfully buffers food supplies.
   - **The Offering Paradox:** Because offerings are almost exclusively desperate crisis pleas (`plea:hunger`), solving hunger cuts offering income to zero!
   - By Y30–50, offered rations drop from 6.1 r/yr to < 0.1 r/yr.
2. **Why does the bot spend only 13.8% of income despite having no cushion?**
   - Income is intensely lump-sum: 90% arrives during rare winter famines, but hits the 100-favor cap or is exhausted on 1–2 crisis casts.
   - In all normal years, income is purely daily prayer: **~5.6 favor/yr**.
   - With small acts costing 5 favor and medium acts costing 20 favor, 5.6 favor/yr cannot sustain even 2 small acts per year.
   - Consequently, the bot sits broke on **82.1% of days**. When opportunities or needs arise, the bot has 0–3 favor and cannot act.
3. **Why does faith never reach a "faithful band" threshold (> 0.5)?**
   - People learn beliefs socially from elders and witnessable divine acts.
   - With the bot averaging only 1.1 small acts/year across 3 bands of ~70 people, a person witnesses a divine act once every ~60 years.
   - Without regular acts or positive cultural reinforcement during peacetime, `god:real` decays to the ambient drift floor of ~0.30.

---

## 6. Recommendations for Owner Decisions (Before Batch C)
1. **Prayer Income Scaling:** Daily prayer needs to reward consistent piety, not just crisis desperation. If a baseline population of 70 people is to generate ~150 favor/yr (target ~24 small acts), prayer income per person needs a ~10x to 15x multiplier or regular seasonal rites must generate baseline favor.
2. **Favor Cap Adjustment:** A 100-favor cap clips famine offerings and prevents saving for large acts (Weather 60 + Heal 50 = 110). Raising the cap to 200–250 or implementing a soft cap would allow storing crisis generosity for long-term guidance.
3. **Belief Reinforcement:** Small acts (omens, nudges) should give a direct, localized bump to `god:real` in witnesses and camp members, creating a positive feedback loop: acts $\rightarrow$ higher faith $\rightarrow$ more prayer income $\rightarrow$ more acts.

---
**Status:** M2 complete. Stopping here as instructed for owner decisions on favor cap, income, and faith growth before Batch C.

## 5. M2c: Belief Growth & The Feedback Trap

### Belief & Favor Trajectory Over Time (40 Worlds)

| Year | Mean `god:real` | Believers (> 0.5) | Answers Norm | Kind Norm | Favor Pool | Food Offered (r/yr) |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Y1** | 0.24 | 4.7% | 0.10 | 0.01 | 4.1 | 0.1 |
| **Y10** | **0.35** | **13.2%** | 0.32 | 0.02 | 21.6 | 6.1 |
| **Y20** | 0.32 | 5.5% | 0.35 | 0.06 | 14.1 | 1.2 |
| **Y30** | 0.29 | 0.1% | 0.34 | 0.08 | 0.6 | 0.0 |
| **Y40** | 0.31 | 5.3% | 0.37 | 0.10 | 0.0 | 0.2 |
| **Y50** | **0.30** | **0.3%** | 0.37 | 0.12 | 0.0 | 0.1 |

### Diagnosis of the Feedback Trap

1. **Why does belief peak at Y10 and then stagnate/decay?**
   - Early in the simulation (Y1–10), bands experience initial winter food shortages. Unprepared camps make desperate hunger offerings and pray.
   - When the active skilful bot intervenes with plant/animal bounties and winter weather shifts, it successfully buffers food supplies.
   - **The Offering Paradox:** Because offerings are almost exclusively desperate crisis pleas (`plea:hunger`), solving hunger cuts offering income to zero!
   - By Y30–50, offered rations drop from 6.1 r/yr to < 0.1 r/yr.
2. **Why does the bot spend only 13.8% of income despite having no cushion?**
   - Income is intensely lump-sum: 90% arrives during rare winter famines, but hits the 100-favor cap or is exhausted on 1–2 crisis casts.
   - In all normal years, income is purely daily prayer: **~5.6 favor/yr**.
   - With small acts costing 5 favor and medium acts costing 20 favor, 5.6 favor/yr cannot sustain even 2 small acts per year.
   - Consequently, the bot sits broke on **82.1% of days**. When opportunities or needs arise, the bot has 0–3 favor and cannot act.
3. **Why does faith never reach a "faithful band" threshold (> 0.5)?**
   - People learn beliefs socially from elders and witnessable divine acts.
   - With the bot averaging only 1.1 small acts/year across 3 bands of ~70 people, a person witnesses a divine act once every ~60 years.
   - Without regular acts or positive cultural reinforcement during peacetime, `god:real` decays to the ambient drift floor of ~0.30.

---

## 6. Recommendations for Owner Decisions (Before Batch C)
1. **Prayer Income Scaling:** Daily prayer needs to reward consistent piety, not just crisis desperation. If a baseline population of 70 people is to generate ~150 favor/yr (target ~24 small acts), prayer income per person needs a ~10x to 15x multiplier or regular seasonal rites must generate baseline favor.
2. **Favor Cap Adjustment:** A 100-favor cap clips famine offerings and prevents saving for large acts (Weather 60 + Heal 50 = 110). Raising the cap to 200–250 or implementing a soft cap would allow storing crisis generosity for long-term guidance.
3. **Belief Reinforcement:** Small acts (omens, nudges) should give a direct, localized bump to `god:real` in witnesses and camp members, creating a positive feedback loop: acts $\rightarrow$ higher faith $\rightarrow$ more prayer income $\rightarrow$ more acts.

---
**Status:** M2 complete. Stopping here as instructed for owner decisions on favor cap, income, and faith growth before Batch C.

M2 is mostly good; I'd grade it B+. The pacing and belief diagnosis is the most useful finding of the whole god project so far. One part overreaches.

**The overreach.** Gemini says the idle world is smaller because of "runaway theft and violence". That rests on raw totals (6,551 vs 2,840 thefts), which a few extreme worlds dominate. Its own paired method from M1 found the thefts and violent deaths to be noise. Fertility is unchanged, so the idle world's 15% fewer births remain probable but unexplained. I'll send that back for a proper paired check. It isn't urgent.

**The real finding: the god is stuck in a broken loop.** The game loop should be: the god acts → people see it → belief grows → devotion → favor → the god acts again. It breaks in two places.

1. **Devotion only happens in crises.** Almost all favor comes from desperate gifts during famines. When the god solves famines, its income disappears; Gemini calls this the "offering paradox". In normal years income is about 5–6 favor a year, about one omen. So even the active skilful god is broke 82% of days. It does about 1 small act a year against a target of 24, and about 0.07 large acts against a target of 1.
2. **Acts are too rare to be seen.** A person witnesses a divine act about once every 60 years. So belief peaks around year 10 at 0.35, then sinks back to about 0.30, and almost nobody ends up a true believer.

That's actually realistic: religion surges in crises and fades in comfort. But as a game, it means the player barely gets to play.

**Decisions for you** (my recommendation first in each):

1. **Everyday devotion.** Believers also pray and give thanks in good times. That's learned the same way: if thanks seemed to be followed by good fortune, the habit grows. It gives a steady income that grows with faith, so a faithful band supports a busy god and a doubtful one a quiet god. **Recommend: yes.** It's natural (thanksgiving is the counterpart of the desperate plea) and it fixes the paradox.
2. **The cap.** Options:
   - **(a) A bigger cap:** about 3× today, so the god can bank one big act plus some small ones.
   - **(b) No hard cap:** stored favor above what your believers can sustain slowly leaks away.

   **Recommend (b).** A famine's burst of devotion isn't thrown away; it just can't be hoarded forever.
3. **How fast should faith grow under a responsive god?** For example: a god who acts visibly and helpfully wins over most of a band within about 10–20 years, about half a generation. A god who does nothing never does. **This is your call**, because it sets the pace of the whole early game.
4. **Pacing should scale with faith**, not one fixed target:

   | Stage | Small acts | Large acts |
   |---|---|---|
   | New god, few believers | About 1 a month | Rare |
   | Faithful band | Weekly | About 1 a year |

   **Recommend: yes.** Earning faith becomes the progression.

Answer 1–4 (and give a number for 3) and I'll turn it into Gemini's next brief, including the idle-world recheck.

On 1: yes, and I think that already happens emergently, with no new rule.
- **Credit is weighted by surprise.** A plea answered when things were desperate counts a lot; ordinary good fortune counts little.
- **So comfort quietly weakens faith.** When life is easy, good times are expected and earn the god little credit. There are fewer crises, so fewer pleas, so fewer answered prayers to feed belief.
- **Thanksgiving still adds a steady base**, but only for people who already believe, and it fades if the god stops showing itself.

So easy times mean less religion, through the same learning as everything else. We measure it rather than force it. If it doesn't show up, we look again.

## 3. How I'd think about belief

The sim can already represent your idea without inventing much. The core is to separate **how strongly someone believes** from **what they believe**.

**1. Strength, per person:** from "nothing's out there" through "something's out there" to "devout". It's already a number per person (`god:real`). To make it readable for you and the player, I'd label rough bands:

| Band | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Skeptic | Low belief, maybe actively doubting |
| Open | "Something's out there" |
| Believer | Prays, thanks, offers |
| Devout | Believer with strong practice, and the one others learn from |

**2. Content, per person:** what they think the god is like and wants, such as "punishes theft", "loves generosity", "demands gifts", "is cruel", "answers". These are already learned per person, and they differ, because each person saw different things, heard different gossip and has a different temperament (credulity, openness).

**3. Religion is shared content plus shared practice.** One generation can easily go from atheist to "something's out there", like you said. A full religion needs content that has become shared and stable, plus regular rites, and that takes inheritance and repetition over generations. Later layers (taboos turning into customs, a prophet, maybe priests) build on that consolidation. So "a full religion" comes from the same learning over time, not from a switch.

**Diversity happens naturally:**
- **Temperament:** credulous people convert fast, and the hard-headed stay skeptics.
- **Experience:** whoever saw the omen believes more than whoever only heard about it.
- **Personal events:** a mother whose child died during an unanswered prayer can lose her faith in a day.
- **Families and camps drift differently.** That's the seed of sects. Much later, belief could count towards peoples splitting apart.

**Fast change, as you said:**
- **Idle god:** with no signs, belief fades back towards the background within about one generation, faster for the less credulous.
- **Inconsistent god:** if it rewards theft one year and punishes it the next, people get confused or doubt; some keep the old beliefs and some take up the new ones, which is diversity again.
- **Single events:** one dramatic event can convert or break individuals, while the population average moves more slowly.

**Targets I'd propose:**

| Situation | After about one generation (25 years) |
|---|---|
| Responsive, visible god | Most people are Open or Believer, about 10–20% Devout, and a lasting Skeptic minority of about 10–20% |
| No god | Back to background belief |
| Any | Beliefs about what the god wants differ measurably between people and between camps, never unanimous |
| Comfortable times | Belief and practice fall off unless the god keeps showing itself |

We'd measure these like everything else (paired, with confidence ranges), plus distributions: the share of people in each band, and how far belief content differs within a camp and between camps.

**What would need building:**
- **Thanksgiving devotion,** learned (your #1, my rec).
- **The leaky favor bank** (#2b).
- **Devout people teaching more strongly:** their beliefs spread more in conversation, the way charismatic people's do now.
- **The measurements above.**
- **Pacing that scales with faith** (#4).

The bands themselves are labels for reading the results, not new rules.

If these targets feel right, I'll write the brief for Gemini, along with the paired recheck of why the idle world is smaller. Any changes to the targets, especially the skeptic share and the 10–20% devout?

# T11 brief — devotion, the favor bank, and living belief

For: Gemini. From: Claude and the owner. Date: 2026-10-13.
Read first: `AGENTS.md` (incl. "Don't waste runs"), `docs/reports/M2.md`, and the "Decisions 2026-10-13" section at
the end of `docs/GOD-LAYER.md`. Branch `task/T11` from `task/T10B`. Don't merge to master.
Standard of evidence: paired 40-world comparisons vs `godoff`, every claim as "+a% (95% CI b to c, 40 worlds)".
Effects whose CI barely clears zero are "probable", not settled, unless other metrics agree.

## Review of M2 (short)
Accepted, with one correction. The pacing/belief diagnosis (crisis-only income, the "offering paradox", acts too
rare to be seen) is excellent. But M2a's "true driver: theft and violence spirals" rests on **raw totals**
(6,551 vs 2,840 thefts), which a few worlds dominate; your own paired M1 numbers call idle thefts and violent
deaths noise. Don't explain a paired result with raw totals. Redo it as D0 below.

---

## D0. Idle-world deficit, properly (measure only, reuse existing runs)
Idle vs god-off: pop −18%, births −15%, techs −21% (paired, M1), while fertility per woman is unchanged (M2).
Births fall with normal fertility ⇒ fewer women of reproductive age, or women spending fewer years in a union.
With paired CIs: deaths by cause and age group (especially women 15-44), adult women alive per year, share of
women 15-44 married, separations, out-migration of whole households. Name the driver only if its paired CI
excludes zero and its size can account for the births gap.

## D1. Everyday devotion: thanksgiving (owner decision)
Believers also pray and give thanks in good times, not only in crises.
- It's a learned habit, like everything else: a thanks followed by good fortune strengthens it, a thanks followed
  by nothing (or by a blow) weakens it. Value = belief × learned return of thanking (`god:thank`), in the Decider.
- Thanks-giving is witnessed and gives favor weighted by the person's belief, steady and small.
- Credit stays weighted by surprise, so in comfortable times good fortune earns little and devotion should thin
  out on its own (owner: easy times may mean less prayer — **emergent, not a rule**). Measure whether it happens.

## D2. The favor bank leaks instead of capping (owner decision: option b)
Remove the hard `FavorCap` clip. Favor above what the believers can sustain (`Σ god:real × k`) leaks away slowly
each day (a proportional decay of the excess). Famine bursts are kept for a while instead of thrown away, but
can't be hoarded forever. Disclose `k` and the leak rate.

## D3. Living belief: strength, content, diversity (owner decision)
Belief has two parts that must both be visible:
- **Strength** per person (`god:real`), read in four bands for reporting only (not new rules): skeptic (< 0.3),
  open (0.3-0.6), believer (0.6-0.8), devout (> 0.8 and practising: prays/thanks/offers).
- **Content** per person: the `god:<act>` profile, `god:kind`, `god:answers`.
Changes:
- **The devout teach more strongly**: in `SocialLearning`, a speaker's `god:` topics are copied with weight scaled by
  their devotion (as charisma and following already scale it). Nothing else new: temperament (credulity,
  openness), experience (who saw what) and personal events already create diversity.
- **Personal shocks**: a death in the family during an unanswered plea should be able to break an individual's
  faith quickly (large `god:real` / `god:answers` drop for that person), and a dramatic answered plea should be
  able to convert one. Check whether existing learning already does this before adding anything.

## D4. Pacing scales with faith (owner decision)
Targets are no longer one fixed number:
| Stage | Small acts (omen, nudge) | Medium (bounty) | Large (weather, heal, lightning, blessed birth) |
|---|---|---|---|
| new god, few believers | ~1 a month | rare | rare |
| faithful band (~30, most believers) | ~weekly | a few a year | ~1 a year |
Report favor income and acts per year against the stage the band is actually in.

## Owner targets to measure (not to tune toward blindly; report each with CIs)
| Situation | After ~1 generation (25 y) |
|---|---|
| responsive, visible god (active skilful bot) | most people open or believer; ~10-20% devout; a lasting skeptic minority ~10-20% |
| no god (idle) | back to background belief |
| any | the `god:<act>` profile differs measurably between people and between camps (never unanimous) |
| comfortable times | belief and practice fall off unless the god keeps showing itself |
| idle god after years of activity | believers fall back within ~1 generation, faster for the less credulous |
New measures: share of adults in each band (Y1, 10, 25, 50); spread of `god:<act>` within a camp (std dev) and
between camps of the same people; devotion acts per adult per year by season and by how fed the camp is.
Also one **"god goes quiet" run**: active skilful for 25 years, then idle for 25 (both sets) for the last row.

## Runs (only these)
God-off identity check on 5 seeds. Idle (new code) and active skilful (new code), both sets. The god-goes-quiet run,
both sets. Unit tests once at the end. D0 reuses existing runs.

Report `docs/reports/T11.md`: D0-D4, then the targets table with CIs and a plain verdict per row (met / not met /
not measured). Then **stop**: the owner reviews before Batch C (gods as patterns).

# Anthro handoff (2026-10-14)

Start here if you are a new agent, or the owner on a new tool/account. Everything the project needs is in this
repo; nothing depends on any AI account.

## What to read, in order
1. `AGENTS.md` — the design rules, how to build/run/test, the run-efficiency rules, the workflow.
2. `docs/agent-memory/` — the owner's standing preferences and project state that Claude kept as memory:
   design principles, balance target (survival hard without a god), realism-not-exactness, "base sim before god",
   and the running state/queue. Treat them as the owner's instructions.
3. `docs/PLANNING.md` — the vision and decided design. `docs/REFLECTION.md` — where we are vs the plan.
4. `docs/GOD-LAYER.md` — the god layer design plus every dated decision since (2026-10-08 … 10-13).
5. The latest brief and reports: `docs/T11-BRIEF.md` (next task), `docs/reports/` (T0 … M2 and Claude's reviews).
6. `docs/PROGRESS.md` (tail) — the base-sim history and its readiness review.

## State
- **Base sim:** done and passed its readiness review (build v80, commit 786a739 on master).
- **God layer (Phase 1):** built on stacked branches `task/T0-baseline` … `task/T10B` (not merged). Belief,
  prayers (outcome-ended, no timers), offerings (learned; shared feasts; escalated plea; grave goods; cultural seed),
  5 powers, credit/blame by misinterpretation, relief learning, nudges as weights, Heal/Lightning, bots
  (none/kind/cruel/skilful). God-off switch reproduces the base game byte-for-byte.
- **Next:** `docs/T11-BRIEF.md` (thanksgiving, leaky favor bank, living belief, pacing by faith, idle-deficit
  recheck). Then Batch C of `docs/T10-BRIEF.md` (gods as patterns), then merge "god core v1" to master, then
  Phase 2 (one band of ~30 + god tests), Phase 3 (sim↔Unity API), Phase 4 (Unity slice). Plan:
  see the end of this file.
- **Measurement standard:** paired per-seed comparison vs `runs/godoff_*` / `godoff2_*`, 40 worlds, 95% bootstrap
  CI (`Anthro.Demog/tools/paired_cmp.py`). With 20 unpaired worlds, differences under ~25% are noise.

## Lessons about working with agents on this project
- Agents tend to: report PASS without numbers; spin drops; tune numbers until checks pass; use timers/hard gates/
  overrides instead of learned mechanisms; restate old numbers from memory. Briefs with explicit acceptance checks,
  batch-and-stop, and an independent reviewer fixed most of this.
- The owner decides anything that changes how the world works or what people value; agents propose.

## Plan to Unity (approved 2026-10-07)
Phase 1 god core (finishing) → Phase 2 milestone scenario + god tests → Phase 3 `Anthro.Sim/Api/` (read-only
snapshot per tick, event stream from the chronicle, command input for powers/prayer answers/time controls,
save/load + determinism check; `Person.X/Y` is cell-level, in-camp placement is a Unity job) → Phase 4 Unity 6.3
simple-shapes slice (map, camps, people doing verbs, notifications, prayer panel, power targeting, person inspector).
